messages:
inc-bot: :rotating_light: INCIDENT ALERT: ZephyrHealth (single-tenant) streaming sessions p99 spike > 5s. Pager notified: @sam oncall. Auto-runbook started.

sam: saw the page, jumping in. quick status?

maria: looking at console now — p95 ~1.1s but p99 jumping to ~6.6s over the last 4m on streaming endpoints for tenant=zephyrhealth. Error rates stable, no 5xx. Looks like stall/slow token emission rather than model errors.

sam: got it. Repro first: most affected sessions are long-prefix chat with repeated system tokens. High concurrency from a single IP pool. Could be kvcache thrash or prefix fanout.

kai: pulling runtime traces. Observing a spike in kv_cache_miss_rate and large num_prefix_keys for tenant zephyrhealth. Also see many sessions hitting the same long prompt template which forces cache invalidation due to user-specific tokens.

ashley: customer on support channel reporting many aborted streams and a drop in UX (clients show spinning "waiting for response"). They see this starting ~2026-03-15T09:12Z.

sam: thanks. Immediate mitigation plan: 1) throttle tenant concurrency slightly 2) enable streaming fallback to lower-throughput model variant 3) clear tenant-specific KV cache keys 4) restart a subset of runtime pods to flush stuck streams.

maria: confirm we can throttle via rate-limiter API. I can bump tenant concurrency_limit down from 150 -> 60 for 10 minutes as a circuit breaker. That will reduce hotfanout.

sam: do it. Also prepare curl to switch model for zephyrhealth routes to a quantized variant (lower memory but faster tokens) — if we serve via same model family it should preserve result quality.

maria: applying limiter now:

```bash
curl -X POST https://control-plane.internal/tenants/zephyrhealth/config \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN' \
  -d '{"streaming_concurrency_limit":60, "concurrency_window_s":60}'
```

maria: response 200. limiter active. metrics should reflect within a minute.

kai: will patch routing to fallback model on canary: set route override -> model: redwood-q8b-variant. Command:

```bash
kubectl -n runtime exec deploy/routing-ctrl -- curl -X POST http://localhost:8080/override \
  -d '{"tenant":"zephyrhealth","route":"/v1/stream","model":"redwood-q8b-variant","reason":"emergency-fallback"}'
```

kai: pushing canary to 2 routing pods now.

inc-bot: update: limiter set by maria at 1823456910. routing canary started by kai at 1823456980.

neil: fetching pod logs for runtime-worker-2 to see streaming stalls:

```
kubectl -n runtime logs runtime-worker-2 -c worker | tail -n 200 | grep "emit_token_delay" -A2
[2026-03-15T09:13:22Z] emit_token_delay=450ms session=abcd tenant=zephyrhealth prefix_keys=184
[2026-03-15T09:13:23Z] emit_token_delay=1200ms session=efgh tenant=zephyrhealth prefix_keys=190
```

maria: those delays line up with the p99. prefix_keys ~180-200 is high; our kvcache is thrashing for those sessions. Also I see KV store CPU spike on node kvc-3.

sam: ok. Kai, can we temporarily clear tenant-specific kv prefixes for zephyrhealth to avoid repeated cold misses? We need to be careful — risk of losing helpful cache but better than blocked streams.

kai: yes. I'll use the admin flush API scoped to tenant prefixes. Running now: 

```bash
curl -X POST https://kvcache.internal/flush -H 'Authorization: Bearer $KVC_ADMIN' -d '{"tenant":"zephyrhealth","scope":"prefixes"}'
```

kai: flush completed 1823457125. KV miss rate dropped immediately in dashboard.

maria: after flush, p99 dropped from ~6.6s -> ~2.2s within 90s. Good improvement, but still above SLO (p99 target 1.5s).

sam: continuing with routing fallback. Any client-visible errors? Ashley: are customers seeing improved behavior?

ashley: support reports partial recovery — some users still see slow streams but aborted streams are down by ~60%. They confirmed clients which hit fallback model reported smoother progress.

kai: canary routing to 2 pods looks good. I'll promote to full routing change for zephyrhealth to reduce load on kvcache-hosting nodes. Doing full promote now.

inc-bot: status update: promoted fallback model at 1823457300.

neil: after full promote p99 hit ~1.3s for a short window, then climbed to ~1.8s when concurrency ramped up again. Looks like limiter needs to stay. Also we have one noisy node kvc-3 CPU at 92% — plan to cordon and drain to relieve.

maria: ordering a cordon+drain for kvc-3 to rebalance KV workload. Command: `kubectl cordon kvc-3 && kubectl drain kvc-3 --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data` (doing now).

sam: fine. But draining will take time; keep limiter and fallback for 10m, then reassess. Also capture heap snapshots of kvc service for postmortem.

kai: taking heap snapshot and uploading to /s3/incidents/zephyrhealth/heap-1823457.tar.gz.

inc-bot: timeline so far: 09:12 alert -> 09:14 limiter -> 09:16 KV flush -> 09:21 routing fallback canary -> 09:22 full promote -> 09:28 kvc drain start. Current impact: majority of streams restored but p99 hovering ~1.6-1.9s.

maria: quick root-cause hypothesis: unusual prompt pattern from Zephyr's client includes very long shared system prefix with tenant-specific tokens that stymie our prefix canonicalization logic. Combined with a sudden high-concurrency burst (they ramped from 20->200 concurrent sessions), KV cache gets huge prefix counts and thrashes, causing token emission stalls.

sam: sounds right. Next steps (post-incident): 1) add more aggressive canonicalization for repeated system tokens 2) add per-tenant hot-key detection and automatic shard isolation 3) improve dashboards to surface prefix_keys per-tenant 4) run a retro with Zephyr support and propose a recommended client-side rate limit.

ashley: scheduled customer sync at 14:30 PT to explain mitigation and ask for any recent client changes.

neil: creating follow-up tickets: INF-7921 (canonicalization), INF-7922 (hot-key isolation), INF-7923 (dashboarding). Assigning INF-7921 to kai, INF-7922 to maria, INF-7923 to sam.

sam: handing to kai for runtime follow-up and to maria for SLO regression alert tuning. I'll stay available until postmortem draft.

kai: ack, I'll own the runtime patch and the hot-key detector prototype.

maria: ack, will tune alerts + ensure we add tenant prefix_keys metric at alert level.

inc-bot: incident transitioned to "mitigated" at 1823460300. Oncall handoff: sam -> oncall next at 1823460400.

sam: thanks team. Final note: no data exfiltration, no 5xx, customer impact limited to streaming UX degradation. Postmortem owner: sam. ETA draft EOD.

ashley: I'll include customer notes and timeline in the postmortem doc.

maria: leaving logs + charts in the incident folder: s3://incidents/zephyrhealth/1823456789/

neil: and saved console snapshots + kvc heap.

sam: closing thread here, will reopen if anything flares. :white_check_mark:
